newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW hedging costs it 1.3 billion marks.
newsitem.headline: VW hedging costs it 1.3 billion marks.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG (VW) said on Saturday it had missed out on pre-tax profits of around 1.3 billion marks in 1996 by hedging itself against falls in the dollar, sterling and mark which did not materialise.

"The number is about right," spokesman Klaus Kocks said in response to a report in the news weekly Der Spiegel, which also said VW had set aside reserves of one billion marks in its end-1996 balance sheet for currency transactions.
But Kocks insisted that VW's failure to make money on the higher mark-value of its dollar, sterling and lira income was the result of its deliberately low-risk hedging policy.
"We can live with the accusation of being too conservative," he said.
Der Spiegel quoted VW currency expert Rutbert Reisch as saying the company had not suffered a loss but had missed out on a chance to make more profit.
